subject: water in space
title: What If You Poured Water Into Space?

scenes.text: What if you poured water into space? It would boil and freeze at once.
Out there, the pressure is almost zero. Instantly, even cold water erupts into a violent boil.
Boiling carries heat away fast. Within a few minutes, lab tests show thin ice forming on top.
The escaping vapor cools too. Below about minus 60 degrees, it turns straight into tiny ice crystals.
Shuttle crews made these clouds whenever they dumped waste water. In 2011, a skywatcher in Germany likely filmed one.
The twist: you can try it on Earth. At minus 30, toss boiling water into the air, and it falls as snow.

description:
What if you poured water into space? With almost no pressure, liquid water boils immediately; the boiling carries heat away, and in University of Sheffield vacuum-chamber tests thin ice covered most of the water within a few minutes, while the vapor below about 210 K (roughly minus 63 C) turns straight into ice crystals.
Space shuttle waste-water dumps formed clouds of tiny ice crystals that then sublimated; a skywatcher in Germany likely filmed Discovery's in March 2011. The same boil-then-freeze trick turns thrown boiling water into snow on very cold days.
What should we run through next?
